points.title: 童年孤寂
points.description: 川端康成出生于大阪市一个医生家庭，幼年父母双亡，由祖父母抚养长大。这段经历深刻影响了他后来的创作风格，形成了对孤独、死亡和美的敏感感知。在大阪期间，他开始接触文学，对《源氏物语》等古典文学产生浓厚兴趣。祖父母相继去世后，他成为孤儿，被亲戚收养，这种失去亲人的经历成为他文学创作中反复出现的主题。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Osaka to a doctor's family, Kawabata became an orphan at a young age when his parents died and was raised by his grandparents. This experience profoundly influenced his writing style, developing his sensitivity to loneliness, death, and beauty. During his time in Osaka, he began to develop an interest in literature, particularly classical works like 'The Tale of Genji'. After his grandparents' deaths, he became an orphan again and was taken in by relatives, a theme that would recur throughout his literary career.

points.title: 求学时期
points.description: 川端康成进入东京帝国大学（现东京大学）学习英文文学，但后来转向日本文学研究。在东京期间，他与横光利一、菊池宽等人创办了《文艺时代》杂志，成为新感觉派的核心人物。这一时期，他发表了《伊豆的舞女》等早期作品，展现了对日本传统美学的独特理解。大学毕业后，他开始专注于文学创作，逐渐形成了自己独特的文学风格，融合了日本传统美学与西方现代主义技巧。
points.descriptionEn: Kawabata entered Tokyo Imperial University (now University of Tokyo) to study English literature but later shifted to Japanese literature. In Tokyo, he co-founded the magazine 'Bungei Jidai' with Yokomitsu Riichi and others, becoming a central figure in the Shinkankakuha (New Sensibility) movement. During this period, he published early works like 'The Izu Dancer', showcasing his unique understanding of Japanese traditional aesthetics. After graduating, he focused on literary creation, gradually developing his distinctive style that blended Japanese traditional aesthetics with Western modernist techniques.

points.title: 文学生涯确立
points.description: 这一时期是川端康成文学创作的黄金期。他发表了《雪国》、《千羽鹤》等代表作，确立了在日本文坛的地位。川端康成积极参与文学活动，与谷崎润一郎、三岛由纪夫等人交往密切。他的作品融合了日本传统美学与西方现代主义技巧，形成了独特的'川端风格'。二战期间，他虽然保持创作，但也受到战争环境的影响，作品风格有所变化。这一时期，他逐渐成为日本现代文学的代表人物之一，为后来的诺贝尔文学奖奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked the golden age of Kawabata's literary career. He published representative works such as 'Snow Country' and 'Thousand Cranes', establishing his position in Japanese literature. Kawabata actively participated in literary activities and maintained close relationships with writers like Jun'ichirō Tanizaki and Yukio Mishima. His works blended Japanese traditional aesthetics with Western modernist techniques, forming a unique 'Kawabata style'. During World War II, although he continued to write, his style was influenced by the wartime environment. During this time, he gradually became one of the representatives of modern Japanese literature, laying the foundation for his later Nobel Prize.

points.title: 国际声誉
points.description: 二战后，川端康成的国际声誉日益提升。1957年，他率日本代表团参加国际笔会，访问多个国家。1961年，他发表代表作《古都》，进一步巩固了其文学地位。1968年，川端康成成为首位获得诺贝尔文学奖的日本作家，获奖理由是'他以卓越的感受性，并用小说的技巧，表现了日本人心灵的精髓'。获奖后，他成为日本文化的国际代言人，频繁参与国际文化交流活动。这一时期，他的作品被翻译成多种语言，在世界范围内产生了广泛影响，成为日本文学走向世界的重要桥梁。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Kawabata's international reputation grew steadily. In 1957, he led the Japanese delegation to the International PEN Congress, visiting multiple countries. In 1961, he published his masterpiece 'The Old Capital', further consolidating his literary position. In 1968, Kawabata became the first Japanese writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, with the citation praising his 'narrative mastery, which with great sensibility expresses the essence of the Japanese mind'. After winning the prize, he became an international ambassador of Japanese culture, frequently participating in international cultural exchange activities. During this period, his works were translated into multiple languages and had a wide impact worldwide, becoming an important bridge for Japanese literature to go global.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 获得诺贝尔文学奖后，川端康成继续创作，但作品数量有所减少。他发表了《睡美人》等晚期作品，探索生命、衰老与美的主题。这一时期，他更加关注日本传统文化的传承与保护，积极参与文化保护活动。然而，随着年龄增长，他面临创作瓶颈，同时经历了好友三岛由纪夫自杀的打击。1972年4月16日，川端康成在煤气中毒中去世，享年72岁。他的去世被视为日本文学的重大损失，但他留下的文学遗产对后世产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: After winning the Nobel Prize, Kawabata continued to write but with reduced output. He published late works such as 'The House of the Sleeping Beauties', exploring themes of life, aging, and beauty. During this period, he became more concerned with the preservation and protection of traditional Japanese culture, actively participating in cultural conservation activities. However, as he aged, he faced creative challenges and was deeply affected by the suicide of his friend Yukio Mishima. On April 16, 1972, Kawabata died of accidental gas poisoning at the age of 72. His death was seen as a great loss to Japanese literature, but his literary legacy has had a profound impact on later generations.

points.title: 文学遗产
points.description: 川端康成去世后，他的文学遗产被广泛研究和传承。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，在世界各地产生了深远影响。川端康成被视为日本现代文学的奠基人之一，他的'物哀'美学理念影响了无数作家和艺术家。1990年代以来，随着日本文化研究的兴起，川端康成的文学价值被重新评估，他的作品被视为理解日本传统文化与现代性关系的重要窗口。如今，川端康成不仅是日本文学的象征，也是世界文学宝库中的重要组成部分，他的作品持续影响着全球读者和作家。
points.descriptionEn: After Kawabata's death, his literary legacy has been widely studied and preserved. His works have been translated into multiple languages and have had a profound impact worldwide. Kawabata is regarded as one of the founders of modern Japanese literature, and his aesthetic concept of 'mono no aware' has influenced countless writers and artists. Since the 1990s, with the rise of Japanese cultural studies, Kawabata's literary value has been re-evaluated, and his works are seen as important windows for understanding the relationship between traditional Japanese culture and modernity. Today, Kawabata is not only a symbol of Japanese literature but also an important part of the world literary treasure, with his works continuing to influence readers and writers globally.

appraisal.zh: 川端康成通常被视为日本传统美学与现代性之间的桥梁，他将日本古典美学与西方现代主义技巧熔于一炉，尤以对物哀的诠释著称，并作为首位获诺贝尔文学奖的日本作家为日本文学赢得国际声誉。不过也有研究者指出，其作品偏重形式美而疏离社会现实，题材多限于上层生活，女性形象常显被动，其对军国主义的态度亦受质疑。
appraisal.en: Kawabata is generally seen as a bridge between traditional Japanese aesthetics and modernity, fusing classical sensibility with Western modernist technique and especially known for his interpretation of mono no aware; as the first Japanese Nobel laureate in literature he won international standing for Japanese letters. Yet researchers also note that his works favor formal beauty over social reality, dwell largely on upper-class life, often depict women as passive, and that his attitude toward militarism has been questioned.

supporter.zh: 川端康成被誉为日本现代文学的巨匠，他的作品完美融合了日本传统美学与西方现代主义技巧，创造了独特的文学世界。他通过细腻的笔触和敏锐的感受力，展现了日本文化的精髓，特别是对'物哀'美学的深刻诠释。作为首位获得诺贝尔文学奖的日本作家，他为日本文学赢得了国际声誉，成为日本文化走向世界的重要桥梁。川端康成的文学遗产不仅丰富了日本文学，也为世界文学宝库贡献了独特的东方美学视角。
supporter.en: Kawabata is hailed as a master of modern Japanese literature, whose works perfectly blend Japanese traditional aesthetics with Western modernist techniques, creating a unique literary world. Through delicate brushwork and keen sensitivity, he reveals the essence of Japanese culture, especially his profound interpretation of 'mono no aware'. As the first Japanese writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, he brought international acclaim to Japanese literature and became an important bridge for Japanese culture to go global. Kawabata's literary legacy not only enriched Japanese literature but also contributed a unique Eastern aesthetic perspective to the world literary treasure.

critic.zh: 批评者认为川端康成的作品过于追求形式美，而忽视了社会现实和时代背景。他的作品多局限于贵族阶层的生活，缺乏对普通民众生活的关注。此外，一些评论家指出他的作品中存在性别歧视倾向，女性角色往往被描绘为被动、从属的形象。在政治立场上，川端康成被批评为对军国主义持暧昧态度，未能明确反对战争。他的文学风格也被认为过于晦涩，难以被普通读者理解和接受。
critic.en: Critics argue that Kawabata's works overly pursue formal beauty while neglecting social reality and historical context. His works are often confined to the lives of the aristocracy, lacking attention to the lives of ordinary people. Additionally, some commentators point out gender discrimination in his works, where female characters are often depicted as passive and subordinate. Politically, Kawabata has been criticized for his ambiguous attitude toward militarism and failure to clearly oppose the war. His literary style has also been considered too obscure and difficult for ordinary readers to understand and accept.

objective.zh: 从历史和文化视角看，川端康成被视为日本传统美学与现代性之间的桥梁人物。他的作品既保留了日本古典文学的精髓，又吸收了西方现代主义的表现手法，创造了独特的文学风格。在流行文化中，川端康成已成为日本文化的象征之一，其作品被多次改编为电影、戏剧等艺术形式。学术界对他的研究持续深入，特别是在全球化背景下，他的作品被视为理解日本文化身份和美学传统的重要窗口。川端康成的文学成就超越了国界，成为世界文学的重要组成部分。
objective.en: From a historical and cultural perspective, Kawabata is seen as a bridge figure between traditional Japanese aesthetics and modernity. His works preserve the essence of classical Japanese literature while incorporating Western modernist techniques, creating a unique literary style. In popular culture, Kawabata has become a symbol of Japanese culture, with his works adapted into films, plays, and other art forms. Academic research on him continues to deepen, especially in the context of globalization, where his works are regarded as important windows for understanding Japanese cultural identity and aesthetic traditions. Kawabata's literary achievements transcend national borders, making him an important part of world literature.

self.zh: 美存在于不完整之中，存在于残缺之中。
self.en: Beauty exists in imperfection, in incompleteness.
